chunks: Munakhkhal ibn Jamil, the seller of slave girls. He narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abu al- Hasan (peace be upon him).
Kufan, weak, in his madhhab there is ghulw.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, referring to Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.بَيَّاعُ الْجَوَارِي: Seller of slave girls, his profession or descriptor
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences indicating a narrator's reliability is not strong
key_terms.غُلُوٌّ: Ghulw, theological exaggeration, often regarding the status of the Imams
key_terms.كَوفِيٌّ: Kufan, indicating he is from Kufa
key_terms.مُنَخْخَلُ بْنُ جَمِيلٍ: Munakhkhal ibn Jamil, the narrator's name

ai.seo_question: Who is Munakhkhal ibn Jamil and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
ai.summary: This is a biographical entry for Munakhkhal ibn Jamil, a narrator from Kufa who transmitted hadith from the Imams Abu Abdillah and Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon them). He is classified as weak (da'if) and is noted for having ghulw (exaggeration) in his theological beliefs.
